chapters.title: GenAI fundamentals: capabilities, LLMs, and context management
GenAI business applications: horizontal and vertical use cases
chapters.text:
Generative AI, and specifically agentic AI, is a paradigm that is rapidly becoming a pillar of modern enterprise technology. Agentic AI entails designing systems where large language models (LLMs) act not just as monolithic text generators, but as distributed reasoning engines, each capable of perceiving their environment, making decisions, and taking actions to collectively achieve specific goals. Among other advantages, agentic AI allows the automation of complex, cognitive workflows. This reduces the need for human intervention in multi-step processes and thus enables the creation of adaptive, autonomous systems that can scale expertise across an organization while integrating human approval in the processes that are most critical.

Among all the emerging technologies in this space, there are many frameworks and their abstractions as patterns that allow for the creation of these agents. This book focuses on the universal architectural patterns that underpin robust agentic systems, while utilizing powerful tools like Googleâs Gemini models and the Agent Development Kit (ADK), along with popular frameworks like LangGraph and CrewAI. These tools are pivotal today because, in addition to being at the cutting edge of the industry, they offer the following advantages:

* They allow for the creation of agents that can reason, plan, and use tools to interact with the real world.

summary.summary_text: This submission is the front matter of a 2026 Packt Publishing book, not a research paper, so no empirical claim or experimental evidence is present. The book is authored by Dr. Ali Arsanjani (Director of Applied AI Engineering, Google Cloud) and Juan Pablo Bustos, with a foreword by Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian. It targets enterprise practitioners building production-grade multi-agent AI systems. The stated scope covers agents, RAG, LLMOps, and enterprise-scale AI architectures. The central promise is a catalog of repeatable design patterns addressing robustness, fault tolerance, instruction fidelity, and compliance monitoring. No methodology, dataset, baseline comparison, or quantitative result appears in this excerpt. The text is introductory and promotional in character. Author credentials are notable (former AWS Head of ML, IBM CTO for Analytics, 4800-plus citations), but credentialing alone does not constitute evidence for the book's claims. A meaningful plausibility judgment of any technical claim requires reading the book's actual content chapters.
summary.general_claim: Structured architectural patterns can enable reliable, secure, and governance-compliant multi-agent AI systems suitable for enterprise deployment.

novelty.reasoning: This submission is not a research paper but rather the front matter of a practitioner book (Packt, 2026) on agentic architectural patterns. No explicit gap-naming against named prior work appears anywhere in the provided text: the foreword uses generic marketing framing ('bridges the gap between theoretical capability and practical implementation') without citing specific prior methods or literature. The extracted claims are biographical metrics from a contributor profile (63% engagement increase, 99.97% accuracy), not research contributions with verifiable experimental comparisons. No prior-art references are named, no baselines are identified, and no methodological advance is articulated relative to any existing approach.

reproducibility.reasoning: This document is a book introduction and contributor foreword, not a research paper with reproducible experiments. The two extracted claims (63% engagement increase, 99.97% workflow accuracy) appear in contributor bio copy at confidence 0.35 and reference undisclosed commercial systems with no experimental setup, dataset, or evaluation harness described. The 'methods' listed are high-level architectural framework names from a book, not implementable procedures. There is no code, no math, no hyperparameters, and no public data reference anywhere in the document.
missing: Source datasets or benchmarks used to derive the 63% engagement and 99.97% accuracy figures

reasons.label: most claims are asserted or speculative (2/2)

claim_corroborations.claim_text: AI systems attributed to Reagan Rosario have driven engagement increases of up to 63% through personalization.
claim_corroborations.note: Three targeted web searches found zero independent sources attributing a 63% engagement increase to any AI system by Reagan Rosario. General industry sources discuss AI personalization benefits but cite entirely different figures and different authors.

claim_corroborations.claim_text: Workflow engines built by Reagan Rosario achieve 99.97% accuracy via self-learning decision models.
claim_corroborations.note: No independent source found referencing Reagan Rosario, a workflow engine, or a 99.97% accuracy figure tied to self-learning decision models. The name Reagan Rosario returns no verifiable professional or academic profile in any search.

trustworthiness.summary: This epub has unknown authorship, no publisher, no year, no source URL, and zero citations. Three web searches found no verifiable professional presence for 'Reagan Rosario' in AI or adjacent fields, and no independent source corroborates either specific quantitative claim (63% engagement uplift or 99.97% workflow accuracy). Both claims read as self-promotional assertions with no traceable evidentiary basis, making the artifact highly untrustworthy as a factual source.

not_applicable.reason: Source classified as non-computational (landscape/survey/pure-theory): no coherent required stack to build, so the tool-stack is suppressed rather than inferring tools the paper does not actually use.
